root_cause.text: The credit calculation in virtio_transport_get_credit() used unsigned arithmetic for the subtraction `peer_buf_alloc - (tx_cnt - peer_fwd_cnt)`, which underflows to a large positive value when the peer reduces its advertised buffer while bytes are in flight, allowing excessive data queuing.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state: "The credit calculation in virtio_transport_get_credit() uses unsigned arithmetic: ret = vvs->peer_buf_alloc - (vvs->tx_cnt - vvs->peer_fwd_cnt); If the peer shrinks its advertised buffer (peer_buf_alloc) while bytes are in flight, the subtraction can underflow and produce a large positive value, potentially allowing more data to be queued than the peer can handle." The patch replaces this with a call to `virtio_transport_has_space()`, which uses `s64` arithmetic and clamps negative results to zero.

This condition compares the corrupted credit value against a limit; if ret underflows to a huge number, this check incorrectly allows a large credit grant.
Assignment of the limited credit, but executed only when the corrupted ret exceeds credit; if ret is huge, this caps it but the rest of the logic still uses a large value if ret <= credit.
Uses the corrupted ret to advance tx_cnt, potentially over-committing credit and allowing excessive data queuing.
Uses the corrupted ret to update bytes_unsent, enabling the sender to transmit more data than the peer can actually buffer.
